subject: Live chat pacing spike — immediate escalation & mitigation steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@bluecart.io>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live chat pacing spike — initial alert

Sanjay — we’re seeing a token-delivery / streaming pacing spike impacting the live-chat integration starting ~07:58 PT. Symptoms: streaming chunks are delayed (95p latency increased from ~120ms to ~1.8s), some sessions are stalling mid-response and clients are timing out. Early estimate: ~20–30% of your live traffic saw degraded streaming during the window.

Immediate mitigations you can try client-side (no code change server-side):
- Switch to non-streaming responses (send requests with streaming=false / response_mode=full) to receive completed responses instead of chunked frames.
- Reduce max_tokens to limit long-tail generation bursts.
- Add exponential backoff + jitter on client reconnects; prefer 500–1000ms initial backoff.
- Increase client receive timeout temporarily to ~12s to avoid premature aborts.

We’ve opened an incident (REDWOOD-INCIDENT-472) and engineering is triaging. Would a 30-minute call at 09:00 PT work to walk through logs and take any requested actions? I’m attaching an initial incident summary and a couple of example request logs to help triage.

Attachments: [incident-summary-20270405.pdf], [request-log-snippets.txt]

—Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Live chat pacing spike — initial alert

Hi Sanjay — Olga from Redwood Support here. Thanks for the quick confirmation. A couple of immediate, low-risk steps while engineering investigates:

1) Non-streaming: set request param streaming=false or response_mode=full. Example curl:
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"...","streaming":false}'
2) Reduce generation window: lower max_tokens to 64–128 to shrink long-tail generation.
3) Client backoff: if you see repeated timeouts, implement exponential backoff with 750ms base and jitter.

We’ve attached a short log snippet showing failed stream handshakes and chunk reassembly timeouts. We’ll keep you posted; engineering will join the call at 09:00 PT.

[attachment: request-log-snippets.txt]

—Olga Petrov

olga_petrov@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivev_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@bluecart.io>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:45:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Live chat pacing spike — root cause & immediate engineering actions

Sanjay / team — Vivek from Infra. Quick summary of what we found and actions taken: at ~07:49 PT an autoscaler config change we pushed to the realtime-serving fleet caused more aggressive shard eviction thresholds (aimed at memory compaction). That change increased KV cache evictions under typical token cadence, which caused a spike in cache misses and heavier backend scheduling, which in turn increased per-chunk latency and caused some streams to stall.

Timeline / actions taken:
- 07:50 PT: anomaly observed in monitoring (95p latency >> normal).
- 08:15 PT: emergency rollback of the autoscaler threshold change to previous values.
- 08:40 PT: a hotfix to the eviction algorithm was deployed to add a short warm-up window on restart so cache isn’t immediately cold.
- 09:10 PT: proactive shard rebalancing and targeted warm-up of the most-requested KV prefixes for BlueCart traffic completed.

Status now: metrics show 95p streaming chunk latency returning to ~160–220ms for affected shards as of 09:40 PT. We’re keeping an eye on tail latencies and I/O queues for the next 6–12 hours.

Short-term recommendations (engineering):
- Keep using non-streaming for critical flows until we complete a controlled canary of the fix across all regions (expected by EOD).
- Where possible, reduce client-side parallelism for aggressive users during the next 24h.

We’ll produce a full postmortem with root cause, timeline, and remediation plan. I’ll include graphs and the exact config diff.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
vivev_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:00:05 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps (BlueCart)

Sanjay — thanks again for the quick coordination on the call. Summary and next steps from Redwood:

1) Impact: temporary streaming pacing spike for ~07:58–09:10 PT (~1h12m), affecting ~20–30% of active sessions for BlueCart.
2) Root cause: an autoscaler config change triggered excessive KV cache eviction under typical cadence (engineering to include full diff).
3) Immediate fixes: rollback + hotfix deployed; shard rebalancing and warm-up done (95p improved by ~90% from peak).
4) Short-term customer mitigations: use non-streaming for critical flows, reduce max_tokens, apply client backoff as Olg a recommended.
5) Next steps: engineering will complete a full canary across regions by EOD and post a full postmortem by tomorrow COB. We’ll also schedule a 30-minute technical sync with BlueCart SREs to review client retry patterns and look for any SDK improvements.

Attachments: incident-summary-20270405.pdf, graphs-latency-20270405.png
Related links: Jira REDWOOD-INCIDENT-472, Grafana dashboard https://redwood.grafana.local/d/incident/BC-1234

We understand this impacted your users and we’ll follow up on account-level remediation (AM will reach out re: credits). Please let me know a window that works for the SRE sync.

—Camila Reyes
